name: Phu Quoc
provinceNote: Phú Quốc is a special zone of An Giang. Nghị quyết 1654, passed 16 June 2025, joined Dương Đông, An Thới, and the old communes into đặc khu Phú Quốc. The new commune-level governments operate from 1 July 2025. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam and Vườn quốc gia Phú Quốc still place the island in Kiên Giang.
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: The night people book is Bãi Trường, the long west-coast sand: the surf, the palms, and the low buildings on the shore. Stay if that sunset over the Gulf is the trip. Bãi Sao is the southeast swim, about 25 minutes from Dương Đông, and the north is the shore the park foothills keep clear of high-rise rooms. Fly from Ho Chi Minh City, or take the boat from Rạch Giá or Hà Tiên.
timeNeeded: A day on the west coast, longer with Bãi Sao
fee: No single island ticket. Beach admission is Check on arrival.
getThere: 1 hour by air from Ho Chi Minh City
bestMonths: November–April, and lunar month 11 to lunar month 4
seoTitle: Phu Quoc travel guide — Bãi Trường, the west-coast night
seoDescription: Stay on Bãi Trường for the surf, the palms, and sunset over the Gulf. Bãi Sao is about 25 minutes from Dương Đông. The flight from Ho Chi Minh City is 1 hour.
intro: You are on Bãi Trường, the shore people book for the night. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam places it on the southwest, about 20 km from Mũi Dinh Cậu to Khóe Tàu Rũ, a gently sloping yellow sand with water clear enough to see the seaweed. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism does not name a colour for Long Beach. It puts the swimming, the food, the cocktails, the live music, the DJs, and the fire shows on this west coast, and it calls this a place to watch the sun set over the ocean. Both descriptions stay. The day in front of you is the surf, the sand, the palms, and the low buildings on the shore.

Bãi Sao is the other swim, not the sunset. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the sand is cát vàng óng, about 25 minutes by road from the centre of Dương Đông, with calm water, shade trees, Robinson huts, and a boat 15–30 km offshore for squid. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism calls it powder-white on one account and white on another, with coconut palms, green hills, and the island’s sunrise, and says to come early on a weekday. All three colours stay. Jet skis, a water park, and parasailing are named there. The prices are Check on arrival.

In Dương Đông, Dinh Cậu stands on the rocks at the north end of the long beach. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the temple was built in 1937 for Cậu, a deity over the waters, to protect boats in heavy weather. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism also calls it Dinh Cau Temple and Dinh Cau Pagoda, and says sailors pray to the goddess of the sea. The day account says the lighthouse doubles as a shrine to the Goddess of the Sea. All three names stay, and both deities stay. After the beach empties, the squid boats light the water. Dinner in town is the night market. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism names the Phu Quoc Night Market, where you choose the catch and have it grilled, with fruit and snacks. The nature account says Dương Đông seafood market. The pearl account says chợ đêm Dinh Cậu. The three names were not shown to be one gate. The street is Check on arrival. The day account says more than a hundred vendors.

Bún quây is the morning bowl: rice-flour noodles with fish, shrimp, squid, herbs, and onion, and a sauce you mix from chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says it arrived from central Vietnam in 1955 as ground shrimp, was called bún tôm until 1996, and is now served through the day and into the evening. Eat it on the street across from the Dương Đông harbour, or along Long Beach. The barrel houses are the fish sauce. Hội nước mắm Phú Quốc describes a dark cockroach-wing colour, salty and deeply sweet, nitrogen 20–43 gN/lít, and the introduction there says up to 40°N. The salt ratio is 2.5–3 fish to 1 salt, aged 12 months, from the Gulf of Thailand, Kiên Giang and Cà Mau waters. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the first draw is about a year, one workshop ages cá cơm than for 15 months to 43 percent, the salt ratio is 3 tons of fish to 1 ton of salt, and output is over 10 million litres a year. The district account says about 6 million litres a year and nitrogen trên 25ºC. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism’s fish-sauce account says the clear Andaman Sea. Every figure stays. Pepper is the inland morning: aromatic and spicy in one account, a floral aroma and intense heat in another.

Give the south its own day. Nhà tù Phú Quốc, also called trại giam Cây Dừa, is in An Thới, about 30 km southeast of Dương Đông. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam ranks it a national historic relic in 1996 and a special national relic in March 2015. Hours and the ticket are Check on arrival. The Hòn Thơm cable car leaves from Bãi Đất Đỏ, about 31 km from Dương Đông and about 21 km from the airport. Sun World Hon Thom says the system is 7,899.9 m and the ride is 15 minutes, and also about 13 km. Both lengths stay. From 1 January 2026 the return ticket is 850,000 đồng above 1.4 m and 700,000 đồng from 1 m to 1.4 m, free under 1 m, with runs at 09:30–11:30, 13:30–14:00, and 15:30–17:30. The earlier Sun World account, applied from 9 December 2023, says 650,000 đồng for an adult and 500,000 đồng for a child, free under 1 m, and hours 9:00–11:30 and 13:30–17:00. Both tariffs and both clocks stay. Weather and maintenance can change them. Kiss of the Sea and Cầu Hôn sit outside the ticket. The show clock and the show price are Check on arrival.

The national park is the northeast half-day. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism calls a short version a half-day trek or a motorbike ride. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam describes a 4-hour tour to Núi Chúa, 565 m, on the Hàm Ninh range. Both times stay. The area figures all stay: over 31,422 ha, split into 8,786 ha strict protection, 22,603 ha ecological restoration, and 33 ha administration; 31,422 ha of which 12,794 ha is forest, plus 929 plant species, on the district account; 36,262 ha on the park office account, 29,596 ha special-use forest and 6,666 ha protection forest. The park office says a visitor fee is collected and gives no number, so the ticket is Check on arrival. UNESCO lists the Kien Giang Biosphere Reserve, nominated in 2006, not a World Heritage inscription. Cục Bảo tồn thiên nhiên và Đa dạng sinh học dates that recognition 27 October 2006. The year and the date both stay. The reserve point, latitude 9.96 and longitude 104.53, is not Dương Đông.
gettingAround: Phu Quoc International Airport is in Duong To. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism names direct flights from Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, and abroad, and gives no minutes for Hanoi or for flights from abroad. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says Vietnam Airlines flies Hồ Chí Minh City–Phú Quốc in 1 hour and Rạch Giá–Phú Quốc in 40 minutes. Sun Group has operated the airport since 1 January 2026. The contact address is Duong To quarter, Phu Quoc SEZ, An Giang. The road minutes from the airport to Dương Đông are Check on arrival. On the island, Vietnam National Authority of Tourism names motorbike rental, local taxi, minibus, and coaches. Hàm Ninh is 20 km northeast of Dương Đông. The park approach is the Dương Đông–Hàm Ninh road, then about 10 km north. The main island is 573 km², 50 km long, and widest in the north at 25 km, one of 36 islands. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism calls Phú Quốc the country’s largest island. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam calls the old island district the largest island district in Vietnam. Both stay.

Superdong’s fast boat from Rạch Giá is 2 giờ 35 phút on the district account. The operator lists clocks and no crossing minutes: Rạch Giá to Phú Quốc at 7:00, 8:10, 10:30, and 13:10, and back at 7:10, 10:10, 13:00, and 14:00, boats III, IV, V, and X, capacity given as 306 and 275 passengers, 26–28 hải lý/giờ. Hà Tiên to Phú Quốc leaves at 6:15, 7:30, 8:00, and 13:45, and back at 8:00, 8:20, 9:45, and 13:00, boats VI, VII, VIII, and IX, 275 passengers. Crossing minutes on the Hà Tiên run, and every fare, are Check on arrival. Clocks can change with tide and weather. Dương Đông is 120 km from Rạch Giá and 45 km from Hà Tiên. Those are distances, not boat times. Nam Du leaves Phú Quốc at 8:00 and returns at 14:00, boat VI. The island office is 187 Nguyễn Trung Trực, khu phố 5, đặc khu Phú Quốc. Ticket counters are listed twice: Rạch Giá at 14 Tự Do, Phường Vĩnh Thanh, and also at Số 01 Lô 4 Đường 3/2, Phường Rạch Giá, Tỉnh An Giang; Hà Tiên at 11 Trần Hầu, Phường Bình San, and also at Số 11 Đường Trần Hầu, Phường Hà Tiên, Tỉnh An Giang.

stayAreas.name: Long Beach
stayAreas.summary: Sleep on this west-coast sand if the sunset and the evening are the trip. Dinner and cocktails run along the shore. The north is the other bed: the park foothills keep high-rise rooms off Gành Dầu.

eat: Bún quây is the morning bowl, on the harbour street in Dương Đông and along Long Beach. Dinner is the catch you point at in the Dương Đông night market, or a table along Bãi Trường. Hàm Ninh’s plate is boiled crab with muối tiêu chanh. Bãi Thơm stops for a coconut, a hotpot, or a seafood platter. Stall prices are Check on arrival.
interestsBody: The west-coast sand is Bãi Trường: the surf, the sunset, and the evening along the shore. Sleep here for that night. The north is the quieter bed, under the park foothills.
Bãi Sao is the southeast swim, about 25 minutes from Dương Đông, for sunrise rather than the west-coast sunset.

interestGroups.title: West-coast sand
interestGroups.summary: Bãi Trường is the shore the night is for. The sunset, the music, and the bed are on this sand.
body: Sleep on Long Beach when the sunset and the evening are why you came. The north, at Gành Dầu, is the bed the park foothills keep clear of high-rise rooms.

blocks.heading: The west-coast shore
paragraphs: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam calls Bãi Trường yellow sand, gently sloping, about 20 km from Mũi Dinh Cậu to Khóe Tàu Rũ, with clear green water. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism does not name a colour. It places swimming, food, cocktails, live music, DJs, and fire shows on this west coast, and the sunset over the ocean. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam also names sunrise. Both stay.

No beach ticket is given. Admission is Check on arrival. A future eco-tourism project, Thuận An, of more than 20 ha on the north of Bãi Trường in xã Dương Tơ, is described as allowed. It is not an open hotel.

blocks.heading: Dương Đông after the swim
paragraphs: Dinh Cậu was built in 1937 for Cậu, on the Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam account. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says sailors pray to the goddess of the sea, and also writes Dinh Cau Temple and Dinh Cau Pagoda. Both deities stay. The visit is the sunset, then the squid-boat lights. Hours and a ticket are Check on arrival.

The night market has three names that were not shown to be one gate: Phu Quoc Night Market, Dương Đông seafood market, and chợ đêm Dinh Cậu. You choose the catch and have it grilled. A closing hour is Check on arrival. Bún quây is the morning bowl on the harbour street and on Long Beach. Bún kèn is a noodle with a broth of dried fish, coconut milk, and a dash of curry powder. The street for that stall is Check on arrival.

Fish sauce keeps every figure. About 6 million litres a year and nitrogen trên 25ºC on the district account. Over 10 million litres a year, and one workshop at 43 percent after 15 months, on the tourism account. Hội nước mắm Phú Quốc gives 20–43 gN/lít and up to 40°N, salt at 2.5–3 fish to 1 salt, and 12 months. The tourism account uses 3 tons of fish to 1 ton of salt and about one year. The association says the Gulf of Thailand. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says the clear Andaman Sea. Pepper gardens are the inland half of the same morning. Pearl stalls sit in Dương Đông, at chợ đêm Dinh Cậu, at cảng An Thới, and at cảng Bãi Vòng. Shop names are not the visit.

blocks.heading: The quiet north
paragraphs: Gành Dầu is the morning when you want the crowds behind you. The park foothills keep high-rise rooms off that beach. The nature account names a flat hike under old trees and a coral garden for snorkelling. Kilometres from Dương Đông are Check on arrival. The 45 km figure is the distance to Hà Tiên, not to Gành Dầu.

Bãi Thơm is the northern tip, still little developed, with a view toward Cambodia. A stop there is a coconut, a hotpot, or a seafood platter. Starfish Beach is the white-sand stretch near Rạch Vẹm. The floating restaurants are on Rạch Vẹm Beach, the next village. The accounts say starfish are in the shallows. They do not name a season. Bioluminescent plankton is described at Starfish Beach, on the south of Long Beach, and on the north of Dat Do Beach, at the right times of year, with no months.

Vinpearl Safari Phú Quốc is the animal park in xã Gành Dầu, not a place to sleep. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says it is open 09:00–16:00 every day. Under 1 m is free. From 1 m to 1.4 m, and visitors over 60, pay 400,000 đồng. Over 1.4 m pays 500,000 đồng. The same account says nearly 500 ha, of which phase 1 is 380 ha. The road kilometres from Dương Đông are Check on arrival.

The park hectares all stay. Over 31,422 ha (8,786 strict, 22,603 restoration, 33 administration) on the tourism account and the NBCA park account. 31,422 ha, of which 12,794 ha is forest, plus 929 plant species, on the district account. 36,262 ha (29,596 special-use forest and 6,666 protection forest) on the Vườn quốc gia Phú Quốc account. Coral counts stay too: 89 hard, 19 soft, and 62 seaweed on the district account; nearly 100 hard, nearly 20 soft, and 62 seaweed on the tourism and NBCA park accounts. UNESCO’s counts are for the whole reserve, not the park alone: 89 hard, 19 soft, 125 reef fishes, 132 molluscs, 32 echinoderms, and 62 seaweed. The NBCA biosphere account says 700 ha of coral and 87 species, and 12,000 ha of seagrass and 10 species. A half day and a 4-hour Núi Chúa tour both stay. The ticket number is Check on arrival. Hàm Ninh, 20 km northeast, has a 300 m mountain behind the village. Núi Chúa, 565 m, is a different summit on the same range. The village plate is ghẹ luộc with muối tiêu chanh.

blocks.heading: An Thới and the cable
paragraphs: The prison walk is the fist monument, a cemetery, indoor and outdoor displays, a documentary, and models of the punishments. The history Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam gives: a French camp, Cây Dừa, in 1950, about 40 ha; after July 1954 the camp stopped; in 1966 it expanded to 400 ha and 400 cells; by 1972 it had 14 zones; from 1967 to 1973 it held more than 40,000 prisoners, of whom more than 4,000 died; 42 escapes were organised. Hours and the ticket are Check on arrival.

Sun World Hon Thom’s two return tariffs both stay: 850,000 đồng and 700,000 đồng from 1 January 2026, and 650,000 đồng and 500,000 đồng on the account applied from 9 December 2023. Under 1 m is free on both. The 2026 runs are 09:30–11:30, 13:30–14:00, and 15:30–17:30. The 2023 hours are 9:00–11:30 and 13:30–17:00. The length is 7,899.9 m and 15 minutes, and also about 13 km. The ticket includes one same-day entry to Sun World Hon Thom, Làng Exotica, and Aquatopia. It does not include food, lodging, diving, walking under the sea, or the Sunset Town extras. A south-island boat to Fingernail Island is a swim and a snorkel. The minutes and the fare are Check on arrival.

cards.title: Long Beach
cards.summary: The west-coast sand: surf, palms, and the low buildings on the shore.

interestGroups.title: Southeast swim
interestGroups.summary: Bãi Sao is the morning swim at the other end of the island. Sunset stays on Long Beach.

cards.title: Sao Beach
cards.summary: Pale sand, calm water, and a forested hill, about 25 minutes from Dương Đông.

blocks.heading: Bãi Sao
paragraphs: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says cát vàng óng, fine like a carpet, calm clear water, and green shade trees, about 25 minutes from the centre of Dương Đông. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says powder-white sand and calm turquoise water, and also white sand, coconut palms, and green hills. All three colours stay. Come early on a weekday. The island’s sunrise is this beach. The sunset beach is Long Beach.

Robinson huts and hammocks are on the sand, and a boat goes 15–30 km offshore to fish for squid and eat the catch on the boat. The fare is Check on arrival. The snacks here are cùi biên mai nướng and rượu sim rừng. Jet skis, a water park, and parasailing are on offer. The prices are Check on arrival. Western and Vietnamese food is served along the beach.

faqs.q: Where should I sleep on Phu Quoc?
faqs.a: On Long Beach if the sunset and the evening are the trip. Dinner and cocktails run along that sand. Choose Gành Dầu if you want the park foothills between the beach and high-rise rooms. No beach ticket is given. Admission is Check on arrival.

faqs.q: How do I get to Phu Quoc?
faqs.a: Vietnam Airlines flies Hồ Chí Minh City–Phú Quốc in 1 hour, and Rạch Giá–Phú Quốc in 40 minutes, on the Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam account. Hanoi and flights from abroad are named with no minutes. Superdong’s Rạch Giá boat is 2 giờ 35 phút on that same account, while the operator lists clocks and no crossing minutes. Hà Tiên crossing minutes and every fare are Check on arrival.
Bún quây, traditionally a morning bowl and now served through the day. Eat it on the street across from the Dương Đông harbour, or along Long Beach. Stall prices are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: What does the Hòn Thơm cable car cost?
faqs.a: Sun World Hon Thom prints two return tariffs. From 1 January 2026: 850,000 đồng above 1.4 m and 700,000 đồng from 1 m to 1.4 m. From 9 December 2023: 650,000 đồng for an adult and 500,000 đồng for a child. Under 1 m is free on both. The 2026 runs and the 2023 hours both stay, and weather can change them.

season.label: Calm seas, Nov–Apr
season.note: Vietnam National Authority of Tourism calls November to April the dry season, with calm seas and clear skies, and May to October the rainy season, with rougher seas and short heavy showers. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam counts the dry season from lunar month 11 to lunar month 4, and the rainy season from lunar month 5 to lunar month 10. Superdong says the boat clocks can change with tide and weather.
